tweets.text: RT @LindaJeng1: I was a regulator during the 2008 financial crisis and later worked in the Senate on Congress' response - the Dodd-Frank Act. I believe deeply in consumer protection, financial stability and economic growth. But the gaps are real. According to the Federal Reserve, six percent of American adults are still unbanked. Black adults are unbanked at 13% and Hispanic adults at 12%, versus 3% of white adults, and 21% of adults earning under $25,000 have no bank account versus 1% of those earning over $100,000. Our financial system still isn't open, and it's definitely not equitable. Meanwhile community banks are falling behind, locked into multi-year contracts with core processors running decades-old technology. The incumbents are comfortable. Everyone else pays for it. Technology is moving ahead with or without the CLARITY Act. After a career spanning both sides of financial regulation, I'd rather we move ahead with clear rules for consumer protection and market integrity than pretend the status quo is working. Let's finish CLARITY. This is the LAST week before the Senate breaks for August recess. Submit a letter to your representative at https://t.co/HBQYj7qHnX today.

tweets.text: RT @Katy_Faust: This little girl is not in the video. She wasn't even born. But she is moved to tears watching her mother and father get married. Why? Marriage researcher and family therapist Pat Fagan once told me: "When a child sees their mother loving their father they feel like their mother is loving them. When they see their father loving their mother they feel like their father is loving them. It is the only time in the human experience where you can be loved indirectly. No one's even looking at you or touching you or talking to you, but you feel loved." That is not the case with a step parent, he said. The child may tolerate the romantic expression. But they do not experience that same circuitous love. More often they feel competition or jealousy. If every child could order their own world, this is what they would say: "I want my mom and dad to love me and I want my mom and dad to love each other." Sometimes that's not possible. Woe to a culture that intentionally denies that to children in the name of adult freedom.
